title: Certificate for: two-point + Voronoi hybrids in R^3 cannot beat the dodecahedral bound

conventions.packing: Lambda subset R^3, |x-y| >= 2 for distinct x,y
conventions.centre_density_c: c = limsup_R #(Lambda cap B(0,R)) / vol B(0,R)   (centres per unit volume)
conventions.density_delta: delta = limsup_R vol(B(0,R) cap union_{lambda in Lambda} B(lambda,1)) / vol B(0,R)
conventions.fourier: fhat(t) = integral f(x) exp(-2*pi*i*t.x) dx   (no normalising constant)

constants.V_HM_definition: volume of the regular dodecahedron of inradius 1 (= Voronoi cell of the 12 icosahedral centres at distance 2)

theorem_B_fcc_constraint.statement: for every admissible f (fhat>=0, f(0)>0, f(x)<=0 for |x|>=2):  f(0) + 12*f(2) >= fhat(0)/(4*sqrt(2)) > 0
theorem_B_fcc_constraint.statement_2: equivalently 12*(-f(2)) < f(0) (the contact cost C_ico at the icosahedral star is strictly below the diagonal term)

theorem_C_barrier.statement: with score B_kappa(v) = kappa*(f(0) - C(v)), C(v) = sum_{mu != v} (-f(v-mu)): (i) at the icosahedral cell B_kappa = kappa*(f(0)+12 f(2)) >= kappa*fhat(0)/(4 sqrt 2) > 0, so (H1) forces V_0 <= V_HM - kappa*fhat(0)/(4 sqrt 2) < V_HM; (ii) mean B_kappa <= -kappa*c*fhat(0) < 0, so (H2) fails. Hence no two-point score yields a bound better than delta <= 4*pi/(3*V_HM).

theorem_D_necessity.statement: if (H1) and (H2) hold with V_0 > V_HM then B(ico) < 0 <= liminf mean B
theorem_D_necessity.consequence: a winning score must be negative on the icosahedral star; the two-point cost is positive there (Theorem C)

no_go.affine_face_count: B = alpha*F + gamma (F = #Voronoi faces): fcc mean F = 12, bcc mean F = 14, every cell F>=4 => no (alpha,gamma) satisfies (H2) and B(ico)<0
no_go.delaunay_vertex_counts: #{tetrahedra at v} = 2*d_v - 4 identically, so affine Delaunay scores reduce to affine functions of d_v; no Euler identity fixes mean(d_v)

this_work.kind: barrier: no improvement for the two-point + Voronoi family
